transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-08 14:30 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Meyer (Redwood SE), Hannah Li (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (Velora CTO), Liam O'Connor (Velora ML Eng), Priya Menon (Velora Platform), Arjun Shah (Velora SRE)

Auto-summary (may be rough): Reviewed p50/p95 TTFT numbers for interactive agent; discussed tradeoffs of int8 vs fp16, streaming chunk size, and sequence-length trimming. Agreed to a 90-min kernel handoff and a 4-hour steady-state run.

Topics: TTFT baseline, streaming vs chunking, kernel choices, quantization impact, steady-state run, security/permissions for logs

[00:00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): okay everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining. quick agenda, do a 10-minute run through of the latest numbers, jonas will cover kernel tradeoffs, then we pick next steps. Marta, how's your schedule?
[00:00:18] Marta (Velora CTO): yep good, thanks. we got the perf sheet you sent. saw some weird p95 spikes last week when we were doing long sequences. want to understand if it's network, model, or the serving path.
[00:00:34] Jonas (Redwood SE): sure, so quick context: the baseline we ran on the pilot is the 7B-ish open model with the rwd-opt-config, sequences trimmed to 512 by default, streaming chunk size 64 tokens. observed TTFT p50 around 210ms, p95 around 380ms when requests are single-shot, but in bursty patterns p95 jumped to 620ms. some of that correlates with KV cache evictions and the fallback to the non-optimized kernel.
[00:01:02] Liam (Velora ML): can you say non-optimized kernel? like the fallback path - is that when we run out of a certain buffer?
[00:01:10] Jonas (Redwood SE): yeah it's when the compiled kernel path that uses fused attention isn't compatible with the current seq len or memory layout, so runtime switches to the generic path. that adds ~120-200ms. compilers can recompile but that causes jitter.
[00:01:28] Arjun (Velora SRE): we saw the same in our logs, there's a big step when a new sequence length appears. sometimes a single 4096 token chat message triggers recompilation.
[00:01:38] Samira (Redwood AE): and that matches the traces in the perf sheet, right? the column "kernel_switch_events"?
[00:01:44] Jonas (Redwood SE): yep that's the one. we annotated a few rows where seq len spikes caused a kernel switch. also chunking strategy matters for streaming — if you pick chunk size too small you increase per-chunk overhead, too big and you delay first-token.
[00:02:03] Priya (Velora Platform): curious about real user mix — our prod mix has a lot of short prompts under 128 tokens but occasionally long batch jobs for analytics. is there a way to route those differently?
[00:02:14] Hannah (Redwood CSM): yep we recommend routing long analytic jobs to reserved batch capacity or the dedicated pool; keep interactive traffic on low-latency lanes. Redwood's routing policy can pin by route or header.
[00:02:28] Marta (Velora CTO): security question — if we do dedicated for batch and hosted for interactive, how are logs separated? we need audit logs in the private plane for compliance.
[00:02:39] Samira (Redwood AE): you can enable private logging to your S3 and restrict access via KMS keys. we'll share the security doc. note sometimes the auto notes say private "plane" — that's a transcript quirk.
[00:02:52] Liam (Velora ML): back to kernels — what are the recommended quantization paths? int8 seems attractive but we worried about accuracy for scoring.
[00:03:01] Jonas (Redwood SE): right, int8 is usually a good tradeoff for latency, but certain attention ops are sensitive. our kernel matrix shows estimated TTFT improvements: fp16 baseline, int8 -> ~15-23% TTFT reduction p50, int4 experimental might give more but risk quality. we'll attach sample evals.
[00:03:24] Marta (Velora CTO): is there an easy toggle? we don't want to retrain.
[00:03:29] Jonas (Redwood SE): no retrain, it's quantization post-training. we recommend running a small eval set to measure regression, and Redwood Optimize can flag quality drift.
[00:03:38] [00:03:45] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) sorry one sec -
[00:03:48] Samira (Redwood AE): jonas, can you explain the kernel handoff idea you mentioned in email?
[00:03:54] Jonas (Redwood SE): yeah, idea is to prepare a focused kernel handoff: we compile a shortlist of kernels that are eligible for our workload (fused attention, block-sparse paths, mem-friendly matmul). then we bring in the runtime engineering team to validate and, if needed, hand off to the cloud vendor or internal kernel devs. this reduces our fallback frequency and smooths TTFT.
[00:04:18] Priya (Velora Platform): who would own the handoff? velora infra or redwood?
[00:04:22] Jonas (Redwood SE): joint ownership; Redwood primes the kernel matrix and tests, Velora runs the 4h steady-state on the pilot cluster and provides logs/access to vendor teams.
[00:04:33] Marta (Velora CTO): sounds ok. follow-up: do we need special creds to give vendor access? legal asks about scoped keys and audit trails.
[00:04:42] Samira (Redwood AE): yes limited time-limited keys and SSO-based roles. Hannah will include the security checklist.
[00:04:49] Hannah (Redwood CSM): i'll paste the SOC2/ISO checklist and the audit-log instructions after the call. note our security docs are in that shared link.
[00:05:02] Liam (Velora ML): quick question on streaming: we noticed chunk boundaries sometimes create short hallucinations or truncated tokens in the middle of a token, is that expected?
[00:05:11] Jonas (Redwood SE): partial tokens can happen if tokenization isn't byte-aligned at chunk boundaries. we add a small overlap (2-4 tokens) to reduce that; cost/payload increases slightly. also the runtime can align chunks to token boundaries to avoid splitting tokens.
[00:05:28] Samira (Redwood AE): we have a recommended config: token-aligned chunks with 4-token overlap and 128-256 chunk size for interactive. for streaming long generation we increase chunk to 512.
[00:05:41] Arjun (Velora SRE): okay noted. what about caching — prefix caching seemed to help last week?
[00:05:47] Jonas (Redwood SE): yes prefix/KV cache reduced repeated context cost by 40-60% for your dialogs. but cache invalidation policy matters; if you pin by user session you get better reuse. the pilot config used a 30-min TTL, we can extend that if sessions are long.
[00:06:02] Marta (Velora CTO): any quick wins to hit our TTFT target of <180ms p50?
[00:06:07] Jonas (Redwood SE): short list: reduce default sequence length to 256 for interactive routes, enable int8 quantization on candidate models, tune chunking to 128 with 4-token overlap, and pre-warm the kernel set for common seq lengths to avoid recompilation. combined should move p50 to ~160-170ms in our estimates.
[00:06:25] Liam (Velora ML): that pre-warm — is that a warm-up job we run at startup?
[00:06:29] Jonas (Redwood SE): yes a small warm-up that triggers compilation for the top 3 sequence lengths and caches them. it costs a few seconds at deploy but avoids later jitter.
[00:06:36] [00:06:45] Speaker 2: (background) they have a question in slack about tokenization -
[00:06:49] Samira (Redwood AE): quick check — did the perf sheet include the streaming chunk config? I saw one sheet with chunk64 and another with chunk128.
[00:06:57] Marta (Velora CTO): it's the chunk128 one we prefer for interactive. but the test that spiked used 512.
[00:07:05] Jonas (Redwood SE): that's likely why the compilation event triggered. big sequence lengths often force a different kernel which recompiles or chooses a compatible but slower path.
[00:07:12] Samira (Redwood AE): ok, decision point: for the next run let's standardize on chunk128, seq_trim 256 for interactive, and int8 enabled as an experiment. agree?
[00:07:23] Marta (Velora CTO): agree, but we want a control run with fp16 too for QA.
[00:07:28] Liam (Velora ML): yes keep the control. we'll run AB tests against our scoring rubric.
[00:07:33] Jonas (Redwood SE): perfect. i'll prepare kernel matrix that lists expected TTFT delta and quality risk for int8/int4.
[00:07:40] Priya (Velora Platform): and about routing, can we have the long analytic tasks automatically tagged so they go to dedicated pool?
[00:07:46] Hannah (Redwood CSM): yes we can put a header or route parameter; i'll include an example in the runbook.
[00:07:53] Arjun (Velora SRE): to prepare the 4h steady run — what metrics do you want us to capture?
[00:07:58] Jonas (Redwood SE): capture per-request TTFT, kernel_switch_events, GPU utilization, memory pressure, and streaming chunk latency. also collect traces for a few sample request ids.
[00:08:10] Marta (Velora CTO): ok we'll do that.

-- mid-meeting deep technical segment --
[00:20:05] Jonas (Redwood SE): diving into kernel choices: for your workload the fused attention kernel yields the best latency but has constraints on max seq len and certain padding patterns. block-sparse kernels help when you have long sparse inputs but are heavy to compile. we noted one spike where block-sparse fell back to dense path since inputs weren't sparse enough.
[00:20:32] Liam (Velora ML): do we have telemetry to auto-detect when it's worth switching to block-sparse?
[00:20:38] Jonas (Redwood SE): we've prototyped a heuristic: if average non-padding ratio goes below 0.6 for sustained period we enable block-sparse for that route, but that requires per-route metrics and safe rollback in case of quality issues.
[00:20:52] Samira (Redwood AE): also worth noting vendor-specific kernels — if you run on, say, Lambda or a cloud GPU they have vendor-optimized kernels that can differ. we had a note about "NVIDA" optimizations in the email — that's a typo in notes but the point stands: vendor kernels can reduce TTFT further.
[00:21:07] Marta (Velora CTO): would that add procurement complexities?
[00:21:11] Samira (Redwood AE): sometimes yes. that's why we're proposing the handoff: Redwood prepares the artifacts and Velora coordinates with the vendor for production signing.

[00:30:12] Jonas (Redwood SE): quick demo of the matrix: (he describes table) column: kernel, seq constraints, expected p50 delta, risk notes. example: fused-attn (seq<=1024) p50 -18% risk low; block-sparse (seq>=1024) p50 -30% risk medium; generic fallback (any) baseline.
[00:30:38] Marta (Velora CTO): thanks, that helps. can you also include expected memory delta? we hit OOM once last month.
[00:30:45] Jonas (Redwood SE): yes i'll add memory delta per kernel.

[00:36:00] Samira (Redwood AE): let's recap decisions and next steps: 1) standardize next run: chunk128, seq_trim 256 (interactive), int8 experiment plus fp16 control. 2) Velora runs 4h steady-state and shares logs. 3) Redwood (Jonas) prepares kernel matrix + hypotheses. 4) schedule 90-min kernel handoff - target Oct 15. 5) security checklist and audit-log steps from Hannah.
[00:36:25] Marta (Velora CTO): good. one ask: include example curl and header that tags long jobs for dedicated pool.
[00:36:33] Hannah (Redwood CSM): will do.
[00:36:38] Liam (Velora ML): any blockers on our side? we need the perf sheet annotated with sample request ids for the spikes.
[00:36:45] Samira (Redwood AE): i'll send that by Monday.

[00:37:12] Samira (Redwood AE): any final questions?
[00:37:18] Priya (Velora Platform): just to confirm the audit logs location — you'll push to our S3 bucket with KMS key?
[00:37:24] Samira (Redwood AE): yes, time-limited role with write-only permissions and CloudTrail entries, details via the security doc link.

[00:38:02] Marta (Velora CTO): thanks everyone. this was helpful.
[00:38:07] Samira (Redwood AE): thanks all. we'll follow up with the perf sheet and kernel matrix. expect the invite for the deep dive.
[00:38:15] Hannah (Redwood CSM): I'll drop the SOC2/ISO checklist in the thread and the example header for routing.

[00:38:30] [00:38:45] Speaker 1: (ends recording)

Action items (auto):
- Samira to send annotated perf sheet
- Jonas to build kernel matrix and expected deltas
- Velora to run 4-hour steady-state and provide logs

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings (NVIDA -> NVIDA, private "plane" -> plane) and some speaker mis-assignments. please reference the attachments for canonical numbers.
